analysis: The only change in this PR is a documentation edit at docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md line 689. The gpt-oss-20b row in the native-checkpoint layout size table now reads bf16 K/V on all 24 layers (3.15 MB fixed state, 25.17 MB full rows per 1,024 tokens, 154.1 MB file at 6,144 tokens). The base row read float32 K/V on 23 of 24 layers (6.03 MB, 50.33 MB, 308.0 MB). No code, configuration, key handling, cache scoping, TTL or encryption behavior changes in the supplied evidence. The edit touches no TB-007 or T-041 control: HMAC-keyed names, authenticated cacheSalt scoping, the 30-minute TTL, AES-GCM with a KEK-wrapped DEK, the disk budget and the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch are all unchanged. The new sizes imply smaller at-rest files and staging reservations for gpt-oss. That would be a runtime behavior change, if one exists, in code outside this batch. If the doc reflects a real dtype change, then the gpt-oss paged KV dtype, storage identity, the historical-attention exact owner/type map and the staging caps (1/8 slot capacity, 1/16 per donor) belong in the Swift source. They were not supplied. That would be a reviewable change in a separate PR or batch, not something this doc diff shows. The doc edit is low risk, and the supplied evidence does not let me verify that the numbers match the implementation. A doc/implementation mismatch could mislead capacity or disk-wear planning. That is a documentation accuracy concern and does not reach the threshold of a security regression. No new attack surface or invalidated threat assumption is identified.
